questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Most hormones of the pars distalis act on another endocrine gland. Which of the following pars distalis hormones acts instead on a gland that is NOT an endocrine gland?

options.text: TSH
ACTH
Prolactin
LH

solution.concept: Targets of the anterior pituitary hormones
solution.explanation: NCERT: TSH stimulates the thyroid, ACTH stimulates the adrenal cortex and LH stimulates the gonads (androgen secretion from the testis; ovulation and corpus luteum in the ovary) - all endocrine tissues. Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk; the mammary gland is not an endocrine gland.
solution.why_others_wrong: TSH, ACTH and LH all stimulate hormone secretion by another endocrine gland (thyroid, adrenal cortex, gonads), so they do not fit the description.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: Prolactin

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Both ovaries of a woman are removed surgically. The blood levels of which pair of hormones will fall as a direct result?

options.text: FSH and LH
Oxytocin and prolactin
Insulin and glucagon
Estrogen and progesterone

solution.concept: The ovary as an endocrine gland
solution.explanation: NCERT: the ovary produces two groups of steroid hormones, estrogen and progesterone. Estrogen is synthesised mainly by the growing ovarian follicles and progesterone by the corpus luteum. Removing the ovaries removes both sources.
steps: Ovary secretes estrogen (follicles) and progesterone (corpus luteum)
solution.why_others_wrong: FSH, LH and prolactin come from the anterior pituitary, oxytocin from the hypothalamus via the posterior pituitary, and insulin and glucagon from the pancreatic islets; none of these is made in the ovary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis and ovary
solution.final_answer: Option D: Estrogen and progesterone

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A drug blocks the release of gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) from the hypothalamus. The secretion of which pituitary hormones will fall as a direct result?

options.text: TSH and ACTH
Oxytocin and vasopressin
Growth hormone and prolactin
LH and FSH

solution.explanation: NCERT: GnRH from the hypothalamus stimulates the pituitary to synthesise and release gonadotrophins. LH and FSH are the gonadotrophins because they stimulate gonadal activity. Blocking GnRH lowers LH and FSH.
solution.why_others_wrong: TSH, ACTH, GH and prolactin are not gonadotrophins and are not controlled by GnRH; oxytocin and vasopressin are hypothalamic hormones released from the neurohypophysis, not hormones whose release GnRH stimulates.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus; The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: LH and FSH

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The anterior pituitary of a person secretes too little TSH. Which of the following is the expected direct consequence?

options.text: Decreased secretion of parathyroid hormone
Decreased secretion of thyroxine and triiodothyronine by the thyroid
Decreased secretion of glucocorticoids by the adrenal cortex
Decreased secretion of melatonin by the pineal gland

solution.explanation: NCERT: TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland. Low TSH therefore lowers the secretion of thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).
steps: Low TSH -> less T4 and T3
solution.why_others_wrong: PTH secretion is regulated by blood Ca2+, glucocorticoid secretion by ACTH, and melatonin is a pineal hormone; none of these depends on TSH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland; The thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Decreased secretion of thyroxine and triiodothyronine by the thyroid

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders results from UNDER-secretion (hyposecretion) of a hormone rather than from its over-secretion?

options.text: Exophthalmic goitre
Acromegaly
Gigantism
Addison's disease

solution.concept: Hypo- and hyperactivity of endocrine glands
solution.explanation: NCERT: Addison's disease is caused by underproduction of hormones by the adrenal cortex. Exophthalmic goitre is a form of hyperthyroidism, and acromegaly and gigantism result from excess growth hormone.
steps: Addison's disease: underproduction by adrenal cortex
solution.why_others_wrong: Exophthalmic goitre (Graves' disease) is hyperthyroidism; acromegaly (adults) and gigantism (children) result from excess growth hormone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland; The thyroid gland; The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: Addison's disease

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a person whose β-cells of the islets of Langerhans have been destroyed, glucose moves from the blood into hepatocytes and adipocytes much more slowly than normal.
Statement II: In such a person, the conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in the target cells is stimulated more than normal.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: insulin, secreted by the β-cells, acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, enhances cellular glucose uptake and utilisation (rapid movement of glucose from blood into these cells) and stimulates glycogenesis. Without β-cells there is no insulin, so glucose uptake is slow (Statement I true) and glycogenesis is not stimulated (Statement II false).
steps: No insulin -> slow glucose uptake: I true
Glycogenesis is an insulin action, so it is not stimulated: II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II attributes an insulin action to a person who lacks insulin, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I correctly follows from the loss of insulin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (endocrine tissue whose secretion it directly stimulates).

List-I:
A. GnRH
B. TSH
C. ACTH
D. LH (in males)

List-II:
I. Leydig cells of the testis
II. Thyroid gland
III. Adrenal cortex
IV. Pars distalis of the pituitary

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

solution.concept: Chain of control from the hypothalamus

solution.why_others_wrong: GnRH acts on the pituitary itself, not on the testis; TSH and ACTH must not be swapped (thyroid vs adrenal cortex); the other codes break one of these links.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus; The pituitary gland; Testis and ovary
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The pancreas is a composite gland that acts as both an exocrine and an endocrine gland.
Reason (R): Glucagon secreted by the pancreas is a peptide hormone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Pancreas: composite gland; chemical nature of glucagon
solution.explanation: Both statements are true (NCERT). A is true because the pancreas has exocrine tissue (digestive secretion) and endocrine islets of Langerhans. R describes the chemical nature of one islet hormone; the peptide nature of glucagon has nothing to do with the pancreas having both exocrine and endocrine parts.
steps: R true: glucagon is a peptide hormone
R is about chemical class, not the dual nature -> not the explanation
solution.why_others_wrong: R is true, so 'R is false' options are wrong; A is true; R does not explain why the pancreas is composite.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas; Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Oxytocin released at the time of child birth causes a vigorous contraction of the uterus.
Reason (R): Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction; in females it stimulates a vigorous contraction of the uterus at the time of child birth. The uterine wall (myometrium) is smooth muscle, so R directly explains A.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are true and the uterine contraction is a direct instance of oxytocin's action on smooth muscle, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: If the adrenal cortex of a person secretes too little aldosterone, which of the following changes is expected?

options.text: More Na+ and water are reabsorbed, K+ is lost, and blood pressure tends to rise
Blood glucose rises sharply because gluconeogenesis is stimulated
Blood Ca2+ falls because bone resorption stops
More Na+ and water are lost in the urine, K+ is retained, and blood pressure tends to fall

solution.explanation: NCERT: aldosterone acts mainly at the renal tubules and stimulates the reabsorption of Na+ and water and the excretion of K+ and phosphate ions; it helps maintain electrolytes, body fluid volume, osmotic pressure and blood pressure. Too little aldosterone means less Na+ and water are reabsorbed (more lost in urine), K+ is retained, and blood pressure tends to fall.
steps: Aldosterone: Na+ and water reabsorption, K+ excretion
Less body fluid volume -> blood pressure tends to fall
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option describes aldosterone excess; gluconeogenesis is a glucocorticoid/glucagon action and bone resorption is a PTH action, not aldosterone effects.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: More Na+ and water are lost in the urine, K+ is retained, and blood pressure tends to fall

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The testis and the ovary are primary sex organs that also function as endocrine glands.
Statement II: Progesterone, secreted mainly by the corpus luteum, acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli and milk secretion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the testis performs dual functions - as a primary sex organ and as an endocrine gland; the ovary is the primary female sex organ and produces estrogen and progesterone. Progesterone, secreted mainly by the corpus luteum, supports pregnancy and also acts on the mammary glands, stimulating the formation of alveoli (sac-like structures that store milk) and milk secretion. Both statements are true.
steps: Progesterone (corpus luteum) -> mammary alveoli, milk secretion -> II true
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements match NCERT, so any option calling either of them false is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis and ovary
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following hormones are secreted by glands outside the pituitary but are directly stimulated by a hormone of the pars distalis?

(a) Thyroxine
(b) Glucocorticoids such as cortisol
(c) Testosterone
(d) Adrenaline
(e) Parathyroid hormone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only
(b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(a), (d) and (e) only

solution.concept: Pituitary hormones that control other glands
solution.explanation: NCERT: TSH stimulates the secretion of thyroid hormones; ACTH stimulates the secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex; LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens (mainly testosterone) from the testis. Adrenaline is secreted by the adrenal medulla in response to stress or emergency, and PTH secretion is regulated by the circulating Ca2+ level - neither is stimulated by a pituitary hormone.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (d) or (e) are wrong: adrenaline release is a stress response of the adrenal medulla and PTH is controlled by blood calcium, not by a pituitary hormone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
In a person, the hypothalamic axons that run to the neurohypophysis are damaged, but the portal circulatory system between the hypothalamus and the anterior pituitary is intact. Which of the following are expected?

(a) Release of vasopressin from the posterior pituitary decreases.
(b) The person may lose large amounts of water in the urine and become dehydrated.
(c) Secretion of TSH and ACTH continues.
(d) Oxytocin continues to be released normally from the posterior pituitary.
(e) The pars distalis stops secreting growth hormone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (d) only
(c), (d) and (e) only
(a), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only

solution.concept: Neural and portal links between hypothalamus and pituitary
solution.explanation: NCERT: the posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus; oxytocin and vasopressin are synthesised by the hypothalamus and transported axonally to the neurohypophysis for storage and release. The anterior pituitary is regulated by hypothalamic hormones reaching it through a portal circulatory system. Damaged axons -> less vasopressin (ADH) and oxytocin released; low ADH -> excessive loss of water and dehydration (diabetes insipidus). With the portal system intact, TSH, ACTH and GH continue.
steps: (d) oxytocin uses the same axons -> false
(e) GH needs the portal route, which is intact -> false
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) is false because oxytocin travels along the same damaged axons; (e) is false because GH secretion depends on the intact portal route. Options including either are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The hypothalamus; The pituitary gland; Disorders
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of events when a steroid hormone acts on its target cell?

options.text: Hormone binds a membrane receptor -> cyclic AMP is generated -> hormone enters the nucleus -> physiological response
Hormone enters the cell -> binds an intracellular receptor -> hormone-receptor complex interacts with the genome -> mRNA and new proteins -> physiological response
Hormone enters the cell -> generates IP3 and Ca2+ -> hormone-receptor complex forms on the cell membrane -> response
Hormone-receptor complex interacts with the genome -> hormone enters the cell -> binds a membrane receptor -> response

solution.concept: Mechanism of action of steroid hormones
solution.explanation: NCERT: hormones such as steroid hormones interact with intracellular (mostly nuclear) receptors; the hormone-receptor complex interacts with the genome and regulates gene expression, leading to new mRNA and proteins and finally the physiological response. They do not need a second messenger.
steps: Complex acts on genome -> gene expression (mRNA, protein)
solution.why_others_wrong: Second messengers (cAMP, IP3, Ca2+) belong to hormones acting through membrane-bound receptors; the last option puts the events in an impossible order (the complex cannot act on the genome before the hormone enters).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option B: Hormone enters the cell -> binds an intracellular receptor -> hormone-receptor complex interacts with the genome -> mRNA and new proteins -> physiological response

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Destruction of the pars distalis of the pituitary would reduce the secretion of glucocorticoids and of thyroid hormones.
Reason (R): The pars distalis secretes ACTH and TSH, which stimulate the adrenal cortex and the thyroid gland respectively.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Tropic hormones of the pars distalis
solution.explanation: NCERT: the pars distalis produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH. ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex; TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones. Without the pars distalis there is no ACTH or TSH, so these secretions fall: R directly explains A.
steps: Loss of pars distalis -> both fall: R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are true and the fall in glucocorticoids and thyroid hormones follows directly from the loss of ACTH and TSH, so B, C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Diabetes insipidus is characterised by prolonged hyperglycemia, with glucose appearing in the urine.
Statement II: In diabetes mellitus, prolonged hyperglycemia leads to loss of glucose through urine and to the formation of harmful compounds called ketone bodies.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: impaired ADH synthesis or release results in diminished ability of the kidney to conserve water, leading to water loss and dehydration - diabetes insipidus; blood glucose is not the problem. Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to diabetes mellitus, associated with loss of glucose through urine and formation of ketone bodies. Statement I is false and Statement II is true.
steps: DI: ADH deficiency -> water loss, not hyperglycemia -> I false
DM: hyperglycemia, glycosuria, ketone bodies -> II true
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I borrows the features of diabetes mellitus for diabetes insipidus, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is NCERT's description.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland; Pancreas
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (action on metabolism described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Insulin
B. Glucagon
C. Glucocorticoids
D. Catecholamines

List-II:
I. Stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids
II. Stimulates the conversion of glucose to glycogen in its target cells
III. Stimulate the breakdown of glycogen, and also the breakdown of lipids and proteins
IV. Acts mainly on hepatocytes, stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

solution.concept: Hormones in carbohydrate, lipid and protein metabolism
solution.explanation: NCERT: insulin stimulates glycogenesis in target cells; glucagon acts mainly on hepatocytes and stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis; glucocorticoids stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis and inhibit cellular uptake and utilisation of amino acids; catecholamines stimulate the breakdown of glycogen and also of lipids and proteins.
solution.why_others_wrong: Insulin is the only hormone here that builds glycogen; the glucocorticoid row is the one that mentions amino-acid uptake, and the catecholamine row adds glycogen breakdown to lipid and protein breakdown - each wrong code swaps one of these pairs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pancreas; The adrenal gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the human female, which of the following together constitute the female accessory ducts?

options.text: Ovaries, oviducts and uterus
Rete testis, vasa efferentia and epididymis
Labia majora, labia minora and clitoris
Oviducts, uterus and vagina

solution.concept: Parts of the female reproductive system
solution.explanation: NCERT: the oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts. The ovaries are the primary female sex organs, and the mons pubis, labia and clitoris are external genitalia.
solution.why_others_wrong: The ovaries are primary sex organs, not ducts; rete testis, vasa efferentia and epididymis are male accessory ducts; the labia and clitoris are external genitalia.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Oviducts, uterus and vagina

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: When a sperm enters the secondary oocyte, the oocyte completes its second meiotic division. Besides the second polar body, this division produces:

options.text: A diploid primary oocyte
A haploid ovum (ootid)
A first polar body
A Graafian follicle

solution.explanation: NCERT: the entry of the sperm into the ovum induces the completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte. This results in the formation of a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid).
steps: Products: second polar body + haploid ovum (ootid)
solution.why_others_wrong: The primary oocyte and the first polar body belong to the first meiotic division, which is completed before ovulation; the Graafian follicle is an ovarian follicle, not a product of the oocyte's division.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis; Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option B: A haploid ovum (ootid)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: At the end of pregnancy, signals originating from the fully developed foetus and the placenta induce mild uterine contractions. These mild contractions are called the:

options.text: Milk ejection reflex
Foetal ejection reflex
Implantation reflex
Luteal surge

solution.explanation: NCERT: parturition is induced by a complex neuroendocrine mechanism. The signals originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta and induce mild uterine contractions called the foetal ejection reflex, which triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary.
solution.why_others_wrong: Milk ejection concerns the mammary glands after birth; 'implantation reflex' and 'luteal surge' are not NCERT terms for the onset of parturition.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Parturition and lactation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Foetal ejection reflex

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a pregnant woman, the umbilical cord:

options.text: Connects the ovary to the uterus and carries the ovum
Connects the placenta to the embryo and helps in the transport of substances to and from the embryo
Secretes hCG, hPL and relaxin
Attaches the blastocyst to the endometrium during implantation

solution.explanation: NCERT: the placenta is connected to the embryo through an umbilical cord, which helps in the transport of substances to and from the embryo.
steps: Function: transport of substances to and from the embryo
solution.why_others_wrong: The oviduct, not the umbilical cord, links ovary and uterus; hCG and hPL come from the placenta and relaxin from the ovary; implantation is the attachment of the trophoblast to the endometrium.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Pregnancy and embryonic development
solution.final_answer: Option B: Connects the placenta to the embryo and helps in the transport of substances to and from the embryo

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A human primary oocyte has 46 chromosomes. It completes its first meiotic division to form a secondary oocyte and the first polar body. The number of chromosomes in the first polar body and in the secondary oocyte, respectively, is:

options.text: 46 and 23
23 and 46
23 and 23
46 and 46

solution.explanation: The first meiotic division is the reduction division: each product receives one chromosome of every homologous pair. NCERT calls both the secondary oocyte and the first polar body haploid, so each has 46/2 = 23 chromosomes; the division is unequal only in the amount of cytoplasm.
steps: Meiosis I halves the chromosome number: 46 -> 23
solution.why_others_wrong: '46 and 23' treats the tiny polar body as if it kept the diploid set; '23 and 46' and '46 and 46' confuse the unequal sharing of cytoplasm with the sharing of chromosomes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: 23 and 23

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Humans are sexually reproducing and viviparous.
Statement II: In humans, fertilisation takes place outside the body of the female.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: humans are sexually reproducing and viviparous. Semen is released into the vagina (insemination) and fertilisation takes place in the ampullary region of the oviduct, i.e. inside the female body (internal fertilisation). Statement I is true; Statement II is false.
steps: Fertilisation in the ampulla of the oviduct: internal -> II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Fertilisation is internal, in the oviduct, so Statement II is false and options calling it true are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Human Reproduction (introduction); Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a male accessory gland?

options.text: Seminal vesicle
Prostate
Bulbourethral gland
Epididymis

solution.concept: Male accessory ducts versus accessory glands
solution.explanation: NCERT: the male accessory glands include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. The epididymis is one of the male sex accessory ducts (rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, vas deferens).
solution.why_others_wrong: Seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands are the three accessory glands named by NCERT, so they do not answer a 'NOT' question.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Epididymis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Both fallopian tubes of a woman are completely blocked, but her ovaries, pituitary and uterus are normal. Which of the following is expected?

options.text: Ovulation stops, so menstruation also stops
Fertilisation occurs normally in the uterus instead of the oviduct
The corpus luteum persists, so menstruation stops
Ovulation and menstrual cycles continue, but sperms and ovum cannot meet, so fertilisation does not occur

solution.explanation: NCERT: the oviduct collects the ovum (infundibulum, fimbriae) and is the site of fertilisation (ampullary region); sperms reach the ampulla by swimming through the cervix, uterus and isthmus. Blocked tubes stop the gametes from meeting, but ovulation and the menstrual cycle depend on pituitary and ovarian hormones, which are normal.
steps: Cycle controlled by pituitary + ovarian hormones -> continues
Ovum and sperm cannot meet in the ampulla -> no fertilisation
solution.why_others_wrong: Blocking the tubes does not change the hormones that drive ovulation and menstruation; NCERT places fertilisation in the ampulla, not the uterus; nothing keeps the corpus luteum alive without pregnancy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system; Menstrual cycle; Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ovulation and menstrual cycles continue, but sperms and ovum cannot meet, so fertilisation does not occur

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following events normally take place in the human oviduct (fallopian tube)?

(a) Fusion of the sperm with the ovum (fertilisation)
(b) Completion of the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte
(c) The first mitotic divisions (cleavage) of the zygote
(d) Implantation of the blastocyst
(e) Transformation of the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle into the corpus luteum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(c), (d) and (e) only
(a) and (d) only

solution.concept: Sites of events from fertilisation to implantation

The blastocyst is implanted in the endometrium of the uterus. The corpus luteum is formed in the ovary from the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle after ovulation.

If Sertoli cells cannot respond, these factors are not secreted and spermiogenesis suffers - R directly explains A.
steps: FSH -> Sertoli cells -> factors for spermiogenesis
No response -> spermatids not transformed properly

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The oocyte released from the Graafian follicle at ovulation has completed its first meiotic division but not its second.
Statement II: The first polar body is formed at the time of fertilisation, when the sperm enters the oocyte.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Timing of the meiotic divisions in oogenesis
solution.explanation: NCERT: the primary oocyte within the tertiary follicle completes its first meiotic division, forming a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body; the secondary oocyte is released at ovulation. Meiosis II is completed only when the sperm enters, forming the second polar body and the ootid. So Statement I is true and Statement II is false (that is the second polar body).
steps: Meiosis I in tertiary follicle -> secondary oocyte + first polar body
Ovulation releases secondary oocyte -> I true
Sperm entry -> second polar body -> II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II confuses the first polar body with the second, so it is false; Statement I is NCERT's description, so options calling it false are wrong.

A. Infundibulum
B. Ampulla

A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

solution.concept: Regions of the oviduct and cervix
solution.explanation: NCERT: the infundibulum is funnel-shaped with finger-like fimbriae that help collect the ovum; the ampulla is the wider part of the oviduct where fertilisation occurs (ampullary region); the isthmus has a narrow lumen and joins the uterus; the cavity of the cervix (cervical canal) along with the vagina forms the birth canal.

Statement I: Spermatids are formed when the secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division.
Statement II: Spermiogenesis, the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa, does not involve any further cell division.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal haploid spermatids; the spermatids are then transformed into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis. Spermiogenesis is a change of form (head, middle piece, tail develop); the number of cells does not change - 4 spermatids give 4 sperms. Both statements are true.
steps: Secondary spermatocyte --meiosis II--> spermatids: I true
Spermatid -> spermatozoon, one to one: II true
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements agree with NCERT (four spermatids become four sperms), so options calling either false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A woman has a regular 28-day menstrual cycle. In which part of the cycle does the corpus luteum form?

options.text: During the menstrual phase (days 1-5)
Just after ovulation, at the start of the luteal phase (soon after about day 14)
During the follicular phase, before ovulation
At the very end of the cycle (about day 28)

solution.concept: Ovulation and formation of the corpus luteum
solution.explanation: NCERT: ovulation occurs in the middle of the cycle (about the 14th day). After ovulation, in the luteal phase, the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform into the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone. So it forms just after day 14.
solution.why_others_wrong: The corpus luteum is formed from the follicle that has already released the ovum, so it cannot appear before ovulation; by day 28 (no fertilisation) it is degenerating, not forming.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option B: Just after ovulation, at the start of the luteal phase (soon after about day 14)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
In the ovarian and uterine events of a normal menstrual cycle without fertilisation, which of the following pairs occur at the same time?

(a) Growth of primary follicles into a Graafian follicle - regeneration of the endometrium through proliferation
(b) Peak (surge) of LH - breakdown of the endometrial lining and its blood vessels
(c) Secretion of large amounts of progesterone by the corpus luteum - maintenance of the endometrium
(d) Degeneration of the corpus luteum - disintegration of the endometrium
(e) Rupture of the Graafian follicle - menstrual flow

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (c) and (d) only
(a), (c), (d) and (e) only

solution.concept: Coordination of ovarian and uterine events
solution.explanation: NCERT: in the follicular phase, primary follicles grow into a Graafian follicle and simultaneously the endometrium regenerates through proliferation (a true). LH and FSH peak in the middle of the cycle and induce ovulation (rupture of the Graafian follicle) - not menstruation (b, e false). In the luteal phase the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, essential for maintaining the endometrium (c true). Without fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates, causing disintegration of the endometrium and menstruation (d true).
steps: (b) LH surge is mid-cycle, menstruation at start -> false
solution.why_others_wrong: Both (b) and (e) pair a mid-cycle ovarian event (LH surge, ovulation) with menstruation, which occurs at the start of the cycle, so any option containing them is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a woman, the pituitary secretes very little FSH throughout the cycle, while other hormones are initially normal. Which of the following is the most likely result?

options.text: Follicles develop normally, but the corpus luteum fails to secrete progesterone
Ovulation occurs earlier than normal because LH acts alone
Menstruation stops because the endometrium is maintained by excess progesterone
Ovarian follicles fail to develop properly, so estrogen secretion stays low and ovulation does not occur

solution.concept: Role of FSH in the ovarian cycle
solution.explanation: NCERT (Ch 19 and Ch 2): in females FSH stimulates the growth and development of the ovarian follicles, and the gonadotropins stimulate follicular development and the secretion of estrogens by the growing follicles. Without enough FSH the follicles do not mature into a Graafian follicle, estrogen from growing follicles stays low, and there is no mature follicle for the LH surge to rupture - so ovulation fails.
solution.why_others_wrong: The corpus luteum forms only after ovulation, which needs a developed follicle; LH cannot rupture a follicle that never matured; there is no source of excess progesterone without a corpus luteum.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle; Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ovarian follicles fail to develop properly, so estrogen secretion stays low and ovulation does not occur

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following cells formed during human gametogenesis are haploid?

(a) Primary oocyte
(b) First polar body
(c) Secondary spermatocyte
(d) Spermatogonium
(e) Ootid (ovum)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (b), (c) and (e) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(b), (d) and (e) only
(a), (c), (d) and (e) only

solution.concept: Ploidy of cells in spermatogenesis and oogenesis
solution.explanation: NCERT: spermatogonia (46 chromosomes) and primary spermatocytes are diploid; the first meiotic division gives haploid secondary spermatocytes (23). Primary oocytes are formed from oogonia and are diploid (they are only arrested in prophase-I); the first meiotic division gives a haploid secondary oocyte and a haploid first polar body; meiosis II gives the second polar body and the haploid ovum (ootid).
solution.why_others_wrong: Primary oocytes (a) and spermatogonia (d) have not yet undergone meiosis I, so they are diploid; options containing them are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option A: (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
In a man, the Leydig cells are destroyed, but the pituitary and the Sertoli cells are normal. Which of the following are expected?

(a) Secretion of androgens falls.
(b) The functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands are impaired.
(c) Spermatogenesis is adversely affected.
(d) The Sertoli cells stop responding to FSH.
(e) The pituitary stops secreting FSH.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (c) only
(a) and (e) only
(b), (d) and (e) only

solution.explanation: NCERT: the Leydig (interstitial) cells synthesise and secrete testicular hormones called androgens. The functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by androgens, and LH acting on the Leydig cells stimulates the androgens that in turn stimulate spermatogenesis. Losing Leydig cells therefore lowers androgens (a), impairs accessory organs (b) and spermatogenesis (c). FSH acts on the Sertoli cells, which are normal, and the pituitary is normal, so (d) and (e) are false.
steps: (d), (e) Sertoli cells and pituitary are unaffected
solution.why_others_wrong: Statements (d) and (e) blame cells the stem says are normal; options containing either are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The male reproductive system; Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of events in human oogenesis and follicle development?

options.text: Oogonium -> primary follicle -> secondary oocyte -> tertiary follicle -> primary oocyte -> Graafian follicle -> ovulation
Oogonium -> primary oocyte -> meiosis II completed in the Graafian follicle -> ovulation of the ootid
Oogonium -> primary oocyte arrested in prophase-I -> primary follicle -> secondary follicle -> tertiary follicle (meiosis I completed) -> Graafian follicle -> ovulation of the secondary oocyte
Primary oocyte -> oogonium -> tertiary follicle -> secondary follicle -> primary follicle -> ovulation

solution.explanation: NCERT: oogonia formed in the fetal ovary enter meiosis as primary oocytes and are arrested in prophase-I; each primary oocyte with a layer of granulosa cells is a primary follicle; more granulosa layers and a new theca form the secondary follicle; a fluid-filled antrum marks the tertiary follicle, within which the primary oocyte completes meiosis I (secondary oocyte + first polar body); the tertiary follicle matures into the Graafian follicle, which ruptures to release the secondary oocyte (ovulation).
steps: Meiosis I completed in tertiary follicle
Graafian follicle -> ovulation of secondary oocyte
solution.why_others_wrong: The secondary oocyte cannot precede the primary oocyte; meiosis II is completed only on sperm entry, so the ootid is never ovulated; the last option reverses the follicle stages.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: Oogonium -> primary oocyte arrested in prophase-I -> primary follicle -> secondary follicle -> tertiary follicle (meiosis I completed) -> Graafian follicle -> ovulation of the secondary oocyte

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following events in early human development occurs LAST?

options.text: Formation of the morula
Appearance of the mesoderm between the ectoderm and the endoderm
Transformation of the morula into a blastocyst
Implantation of the blastocyst in the endometrium

solution.explanation: NCERT: cleavage gives the morula (8-16 blastomeres); the morula transforms into a blastocyst as it moves into the uterus; the blastocyst is implanted in the endometrium; after implantation the inner cell mass differentiates into an outer ectoderm and an inner endoderm, and a mesoderm soon appears between them.
solution.why_others_wrong: Morula, blastocyst and implantation all come before the inner cell mass forms germ layers, so none of them is the last event.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation; Pregnancy and embryonic development
solution.final_answer: Option B: Appearance of the mesoderm between the ectoderm and the endoderm

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A human sperm and a human ovum each carry 22 autosomes and one sex chromosome.
Statement II: The sex of the baby is decided at the time of implantation, depending on where the blastocyst attaches.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Gametes are haploid (23 chromosomes = 22 autosomes + 1 sex chromosome): the ovum always carries X and a sperm carries X or Y. NCERT: the sex of the baby is decided at fertilisation - a sperm carrying X gives XX (female), a sperm carrying Y gives XY (male). Implantation site has no role. Statement I is true; Statement II is false.
steps: Sex fixed at fertilisation by the sperm's X or Y -> II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II replaces fertilisation by implantation as the moment of sex determination, so it is false; Statement I is true, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Total well-being in all aspects of reproduction: physical, emotional, behavioural and social
Only the ability to produce a large number of children
Only physically normal reproductive organs, without regard to behaviour

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A man has undergone vasectomy. His seminal vesicles, prostate and bulbourethral glands are normal. Which of the following is expected?

options.text: Seminal plasma is still ejaculated, but it lacks sperms
No semen of any kind is ejaculated
Sperm formation in the testes stops completely
Sperms are ejaculated, but they cannot swim

solution.explanation: NCERT: in vasectomy a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum, blocking gamete transport. Sperms from the testis can no longer pass through the vas deferens, but the accessory glands still secrete the seminal plasma, so an ejaculate is still formed - without sperms.

Accessory glands normal -> seminal plasma still formed

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Birth control (surgical methods); Ch 2 'The male reproductive system'

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and the frequency of the recessive allele a is 0.1. Of all the copies of allele a present in the population, what percentage are carried by heterozygous (Aa) individuals?

solution.why_others_wrong: Statement (d) reverses NCERT - helper T-lymphocytes fall progressively - so options containing (d) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', AIDS

questions.subject: Zoology

In which of the following situations does the person develop ACTIVE immunity?

(a) A child is given a vaccine containing inactivated or weakened pathogens.
(b) A person recovers from a natural infection by a pathogen.

(b), (c) and (d) only
(a), (b) and (e) only

steps: Second encounter: highly intensified -> R explains A

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A female Anopheles mosquito bites a person in whom Plasmodium is still multiplying only within the liver cells and has not yet attacked the red blood cells. Why is the mosquito unlikely to pick up an infection that can later be passed on?

options.text: Sporozoites are found only in the human blood at this stage
Gametocytes, the stages that infect the mosquito, develop only in red blood cells
Fertilisation of Plasmodium gametes takes place in the human liver
Only male mosquitoes can pick up Plasmodium from humans

solution.explanation: NCERT: sporozoites enter the human, multiply in liver cells and then attack red blood cells; the sexual stages (gametocytes) develop in the red blood cells. When a female Anopheles bites an infected person, these gametocytes enter the mosquito, where fertilisation and development take place. If the parasites are still only in the liver, there are no gametocytes in the blood to be picked up.
steps: No RBC stage -> nothing for the mosquito to take up
solution.why_others_wrong: Sporozoites are the stage injected by the mosquito, not taken up by it; fertilisation happens in the mosquito, not the human liver; NCERT names the female Anopheles as the vector.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common diseases in humans (malaria)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Gametocytes, the stages that infect the mosquito, develop only in red blood cells

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of events in an allergic reaction to pollen?

options.text: Exposure to pollen -> release of interferons by infected cells -> production of IgA -> sneezing
Exposure to pollen -> attack on self-cells by the immune system -> release of histamine -> joint pain
Release of histamine from mast cells -> exposure to pollen -> production of IgG -> sneezing
Exposure to pollen -> production of IgE antibodies -> release of histamine and serotonin from mast cells -> sneezing, watery eyes and running nose

solution.explanation: NCERT: allergy is the exaggerated response of the immune system to certain antigens (allergens) in the environment, such as pollen; the antibodies produced are of the IgE type; allergic reactions are due to the release of chemicals like histamine and serotonin from the mast cells, causing symptoms such as sneezing, watery eyes, running nose and difficulty in breathing.
steps: Mast cells release histamine and serotonin
solution.why_others_wrong: Interferons come from virus-infected cells and allergy involves IgE, not IgA or IgG; attack on self-cells is auto-immunity; histamine release cannot come before exposure to the allergen.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Allergies
solution.final_answer: Option D: Exposure to pollen -> production of IgE antibodies -> release of histamine and serotonin from mast cells -> sneezing, watery eyes and running nose

steps: Linked to vector and transferred alone
Only the desired DNA enters -> R explains A

solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors; Tools of recombinant DNA technology

In EcoRI, E comes from Escherichia, co from coli and R from strain RY 13. Both are true, but the source strain has nothing to do with the way the enzyme cuts.

Source strain does not explain sticky ends

steps: (e) ampR intact in both kinds of transformant

questions.subject: Zoology

Which of the following features would make a plasmid a POOR cloning vector?

(a) Many recognition sites for the restriction enzyme that is to be used
(b) No selectable marker
(c) No origin of replication
(d) A single recognition site for the restriction enzyme, located within a selectable marker gene
(e) An origin of replication that supports a high copy number

(b), (c) and (d) only

solution.concept: Features required in a cloning vector
solution.explanation: NCERT: a vector needs an ori (to replicate; it also controls copy number - high copy numbers are useful when many copies are needed), a selectable marker (to distinguish transformants), and very few, preferably single, recognition sites for the commonly used restriction enzymes - more than one site generates several fragments and complicates cloning. A single site within a marker gene even allows insertional inactivation.
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) and (e) are features NCERT recommends, so options listing them as making a poor vector are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Cloning vectors

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Once a restriction endonuclease finds its specific recognition sequence, it binds to the DNA and cuts each of the two strands of the double helix at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones.
Statement II: A restriction endonuclease separates the two strands of DNA only by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the complementary bases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: each restriction endonuclease functions by 'inspecting' the length of a DNA sequence; once it finds its specific recognition sequence, it binds to the DNA and cuts each of the two strands of the double helix at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones. It cuts the backbone (phosphodiester linkages); merely breaking hydrogen bonds would only separate strands, as in denaturation. Statement I is true; II is false.
steps: Cut is in the sugar-phosphate backbone -> I true
Not merely hydrogen bonds -> II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II describes strand separation (like heat denaturation in PCR), not cutting, so it is false; Statement I is NCERT's description.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 9 'Biotechnology: Principles and Processes', Tools of recombinant DNA technology (restriction enzymes)

RNAi alone, using sense RNA of the caterpillar's genes without any anti-sense RNA
Introducing the ADA gene with a retroviral vector
RNAi using nematode-specific genes, plus cry genes from Bacillus thuringiensis that act on lepidopterans

solution.explanation: NCERT: tobacco was made resistant to the nematode Meloidegyne incognitia by RNAi - nematode-specific genes introduced with Agrobacterium vectors produce sense and anti-sense RNA, forming dsRNA that silences a specific nematode mRNA. Insect resistance comes from Bt toxin genes (cry genes) of Bacillus thuringiensis, some of whose proteins kill lepidopterans such as the tobacco budworm.
steps: Nematode: RNAi with nematode-specific genes (Agrobacterium vector)
Caterpillars: suitable cry genes from B. thuringiensis
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT's nematode protection used RNAi, not Bt toxins; RNAi needs both sense and anti-sense RNA to form dsRNA; the ADA gene and retroviral vector belong to human gene therapy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 10 'Biotechnology and its Applications', Biotechnological applications in agriculture
solution.final_answer: Option D: RNAi using nematode-specific genes, plus cry genes from Bacillus thuringiensis that act on lepidopterans
